latest.text:
Fritz beat Tirante 6–2, 4–6, 7–6 in the final, which leaves them at 1 win each in their head to head. Fritz controlled the start, lost the thread for a set and then won a tight decider without a single break of serve.

Fritz broke for 3–1 in the first set. Tirante saved a set point at 5–2 on his own serve but Fritz needed only 2 break points in that game to break again for 6–2. The second set went the other way: Tirante saved a break point to hold for 1–1, broke for 4–3 and took the set 6–4. Fritz knows he let it slip: "It was a stressful match, … I came out and was playing really well but then let some opportunities slip."

The third set had no break of serve at all, so it came down to the tiebreak. Fritz was the steadier player there and took it 7–3.

Fritz won this final with his serve, especially the second one. He won 73% of the points behind his second serve, far above his 53% average on hard, so Tirante rarely got a chance to attack it.

Tirante kept the score close with his own serve in the last two sets. In the first set, though, he really struggled behind his second serve and won only 17% of those points. That set was gone before the match turned.

All in all, a deserved title for Fritz, built on a strong start and a serve that held firm when the final got tight, which is what makes a big server and complete baseliner like him so dangerous. He beat Norrie in straight sets, got a walkover from Rune in the QF and beat Musetti in straight sets and this was the only set he dropped all week. On the title he said: "I have lost a lot of indoor finals but at the same time I didn't look too much into it, because when I won Tokyo, it was pretty much indoors as the roof was closed a lot, … It feels good to get that one now."

latest.text:
Fritz beat Musetti 6–4, 6–2 in the SF to reach the final. The head to head now stands at Fritz 4, Musetti 5. It was a one-sided match that lasted only 63 minutes, with Fritz on the attack from the first point.

One break decided the first set. Fritz broke for 2–1 and kept Musetti under pressure from there, stepping in to take the ball early. Musetti took the first game of the second set but that was the moment of the match: Fritz then won 5 games in a row from 0-1 down. He needed 2 break points to break for 2–1 and broke again for 4–1, so the last part of the match was only a matter of time.

Fritz won it with his serve and his forehand. Even behind his second serve he won 77% of the points against his 53% average on hard, so Musetti never found a way into his service games. On return he went after the second serve and won 67% of those points, with the forehand doing most of the damage from the baseline. He explained the plan himself: "I was much more aggressive and took on more uncomfortable shots, but against him I needed to do that to win"

Musetti, a counterpuncher, had no answer to that attack. He won only 19% of the points against the first serve and could never put the Fritz serve under pressure.

All in all, a very complete win from Fritz, built on aggression, his serve and his forehand, exactly what makes a big server and complete baseliner so dangerous. He has not dropped a set this week after beating Norrie in straight sets and getting a walkover from Rune. Next is Tirante in the final, who beat Munar in straight sets, needed three sets against Shevchenko in the QF and then beat Tabilo in straight sets.

The key break came in the third game and Fritz served very well while keeping Musetti under pressure. His forehand produced many winners and he finished with 24 winners as Musetti had no answer to his attack. His tactics worked throughout and he reached his sixth final of the year and his first in Stockholm.
